items.title: Using `args` builtin ignores `missing_probes` config
items.body:
Normally, when trying to attach to multiple attach points out of which some do not exist, the `missing_probes` config option is considered:
```
# bpftrace -e 'fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { exit() }'
ERROR: No BTF found for vfs_rea.
ERROR: Unable to attach probe: fentry:vfs_rea. If this is expected, set the 'missing_probes' config variable to 'warn'.

# bpftrace -e 'config = { missing_probes = "warn" } fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { exit() }'
WARNING: No BTF found for vfs_rea.
WARNING: Unable to attach probe: fentry:vfs_rea. Skipping.
Attached 1 probe
```

This, however, is not respected when the `args` builtin is used:
```
# bpftrace -e 'fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { print(args); exit() }'
stdin:1:17-31: ERROR: Unable to get arguments for fentryvfs_rea: no BTF data for vfs_rea
fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { print(args); exit() }
                ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

# bpftrace -e 'config = { missing_probes = "warn" } fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { print(args); exit() }'
stdin:1:54-68: ERROR: Unable to get arguments for fentryvfs_rea: no BTF data for vfs_rea
config = { missing_probes = "warn" } fentry:vfs_read,fentry:vfs_rea { print(args); exit() }
                                                     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

The reason is that argument resolution is done in the `ArgsResolver` pass which always raises an error when arguments of some probe cannot be resolved (e.g. because the probe doesn't exist).

Fixing this was my original intention while working on #4762 but it turned out to be very tricky so I'm instead opening an issue to discuss. There's a number of factors in play here. With #4697 and #4742, the probes with `args` are now expanded such that each probe has a single attach point.

So, when we cannot resolve args, we could just remove the (single) attach point and let `ProbePrunePass` handle it. The problem is that `ProbePrunePass` is only run after `SemanticAnalyser` which is done on purpose (at least per https://github.com/bpftrace/bpftrace/pull/4742#discussion_r2441473681). But, with args resolution unsuccessful, semantic analyser won't find the correct type for the `args` builtin and will fail with all kinds of errors.

Should we perhaps consider pruning empty probes in `ArgResolver` (basically duplicating `ProbePrunePass` but only for probes with `args`)? That's the best I have so far, so I'm eager to hear other people ideas.

items.title: RFC: Logging Updates
items.body:
Currently, we have 6 different log flavors (all with varying degrees of use and for varying purposes):

- `DEBUG` (used 1 time)
- `INFO` (used 3 times - one of those times is wrong and another is in a unit test)
- `WARNING` (used a lot) 
- `ERROR` (used a lot) 
- `FATAL` (used a lot)
- `BUG` (used 17 times)

At the moment, it seems like `FATAL` and `BUG` are used interchangeably and `ERROR` is sometimes used like a `WARNING` and other times like `FATAL` (calling `exit` right after). There are also plenty of uses of `std::cout` and `std::cerr` - sometimes nested inside `bt_verbose` checks.

**UPDATED Proposal in a comment below.**

So this is an RFC to re-work and codify these logging flavors. Here is the outdated proposal:

- `INFO`: log info to the user regardless of log level - like using stdout
- `V1`: log info to the user only if verbose logging is enabled (bt_verbose or -v)
- `V2`: log info to the user only if very verbose logging is enabled (bt_verbose2 or -vv)
- `WARNING`: log info that might affect bpftrace behavior or output but allows the run to continue - like using stderr
- `ERROR`: abort run and log info to indicate that the user did something invalid which caused bpftrace to exit
- `BUG`: abort run and log info to indicate that there is an internal/unexpected issue (not caused by invalid user program code or CLI use)

**Note**: `V1` and `V2` will replace all instances like this:
```
if (bt_verbose) {
    std::cout << "Attaching to " << probe_.funcs.size() << " functions"
              << std::endl;
```

items.title: LLVM ERROR: out of memory
items.body:
There seems to be some combination of tracepoint args, maps, structs, and LLVM optimization level 3, that causes this:

```
# bpftrace test.bt
LLVM ERROR: out of memory
Aborted
```

This is after I set some ulimits to prevent it from trying to eat all the memory of the system, for which it'd get OOM killed. Before running the following, you'll want to do this too:

```
ulimit -v 1000000
ulimit -m 1000000
```

That sets maximums to 1 Gbyte.

Now the program (whittled down from a more complex example):

```
#!/usr/local/bin/bpftrace

struct struct_b {
	int data;
};

struct struct_a {
	int             member_a;
	struct struct_b member_b;
};

tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_futex
{
	@u = args->utime;
	$s = (struct struct_a *)@u;
	printf("%d\n", $s->member_b.data);
}
```

Yes, the program doesn't make sense -- casting utime as different struct. But LLVM shouldn't go run-away with memory consumption.

This program works if I do any one of these:

- Recompile bpftrace without LLVM optimizations (PMB.OptLevel = 0 in codegen).
- Change `@u` to $u.
- Delete the unused member_a.

items.title: Update log messages
items.body:
- `DEBUG`: log info to the user regardless of log level
(like using stdout and comes with file and line number).
No prefix.
- `V1`: log info to the user only if verbose logging is
enabled (bt_verbose or -v) Note: -vv will be deleted as
it's only used in two places in one file. No prefix.
- `WARNING`: log info that might affect bpftrace behavior
or output but allows the run to continue (like using
stderr). Prefix: "WARNING:"
- `ERROR`: log info to indicate that the user did
something invalid which will (eventually) cause bpftrace
to exit (via `exit(1)` or `LOG(FATAL)`). This should get
used if there a multiple errors that need to get logged
to the user otherwise use `FATAL`. Prefix: "ERROR:"
- `FATAL`: abort run and log info to indicate that the
user did something invalid which caused bpftrace to exit.
Prefix: "ERROR:"
- `BUG`: abort run and log info to indicate that there
is an internal/unexpected issue (not caused by invalid
user program code or CLI use). Prefix: "BUG:"

Also update many sites in accordance with the above
schema.

However, there are still many places that utilize
LOG(ERROR) that could be switched to LOG(FATAL) or
LOG(WARNING) but some changes seemed beyond this PR.

items.title: SIGABRT generated when args contains members with bool type
items.body:
If we try keying a map using any `args` member whose type is a`bool`  a SIGABRT is generated:

```
#  grep transport_offset_valid /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/events/net/net_dev_start_xmit/format
        field:bool transport_offset_valid;      offset:48;      size:1; signed:0;

# bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:net:net_dev_start_xmit{@[args->transport_offset_valid] = count();}'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

The top few frames:

```
(gdb) bt
#0  0x00007ffff2448277 in raise () from /lib64/libc.so.6
#1  0x00007ffff2449968 in abort () from /lib64/libc.so.6
#2  0x00000000005aa711 in bpftrace::ast::IRBuilderBPF::GetType (
    this=0x7fffffffd8b8, stype=...)
    at /data/users/jonhaslam/bpftrace/src/ast/irbuilderbpf.cpp:126
#3  0x00000000005aa409 in bpftrace::ast::IRBuilderBPF::CreateAllocaBPF (
    this=0x7fffffffd8b8, stype=..., name=...)
    at /data/users/jonhaslam/bpftrace/src/ast/irbuilderbpf.cpp:57
#4  0x000000000058a995 in bpftrace::ast::CodegenLLVM::visit (
    this=0x7fffffffd890, acc=...)
```

In we look at the `stype` struct in frame 2 we see its size is 0 which leads to the abort:

```
(gdb) p stype
$2 = (const bpftrace::SizedType &) @0x8ada78: {
  type = bpftrace::Type::none,
  size = 0,
...
```

This reason for this is because `clang_parser.cpp/get_sized_type()` is missing handling the clang `CXType_Bool` type so we default the type size to be 0.

I'll push a fix shortly.
